newsitem.title: USA: Judge denies request to release Hamas leader.
newsitem.headline: Judge denies request to release Hamas leader.

text.p: A New York judge on Monday denied a request to free Hamas political leader Mousa Mohammed Abu Marzook or order his deportation, saying the issue was now moot because the government was no longer trying to extradite him to Israel.
The decision by U.S. District Judge Denise Cote put the matter formally into the hands of the Immigration and Naturalisation Service (INS).

The INS is likely to hold hearings soon to determine whether Abu Marzook should be "excluded" under a 1990 law that refuses admission to aliens engaged in or giving material support to "terrorist" activities.
Lawyers for Abu Marzook had sought his release or deportation saying the government had failed to act on Israel's extradition request by a March 28 deadline.
The lawyers had also argued that there was no need for lengthy administration INS proceedings because Abu Marzook "is prepared for that exclusion now."

"Abu Marzook's petition makes no request regarding his release from INS custody," the judge said in her six page decision. "Merely naming the Director of the INS is not sufficient to raise Abu Marzook's exclusion proceedings as an issue before this Court," she said.
Last Monday, prosecutors told the judge she no longer had jurisdiction because extradition was not an issue and that the matter should be returned to an immigration judge.
Abu Marzook must either contest or concede that he was involved in "terrorist" activities before he can be deported.
Although Abu Marzook has agreed to his deportation from the United States, he maintains he has not been involved in or supported violence and denies the allegations.

At issue is whether Abu Marzook will have to enter any kind of plea to INS charges. His lawyers said they believed this might be part of ongoing diplomatic negotiations aimed at finding a way to deport Abu Marzook to Jordan.
Abu Marzook has been held at a federal prison facility in New York for the last 21 months.
He told Reuters in a recent interview he believed a deal had been struck in which he woild be deported to Jordan.

He was arrested on July 25, 1995, at a New York airport as he flew to the United States -- where he had lived for years -- after immigration officials found his name on its "watch list" of people with "known or suspected ties to terrorist activities."
